hints.title: Parent Pointers as Linked Lists
hints.text: Each node has an upward parent pointer. Following parents from p and q creates two intersecting singly linked lists terminating at the root.

hints.title: Two-Pointer Path Equalization
hints.text: Trace upward from p and q simultaneously. When either pointer reaches null, redirect it to the other starting node.

hints.title: Intersection Convergence
hints.text: Both pointers traverse total distance len(p) + len(q), meeting at the lowest common ancestor in O(1) auxiliary space.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Traverses upward along ancestral paths using constant auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Storing all ancestors in a hash set uses O(H) auxiliary space.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Two-pointer redirection traverses at most 2H steps with zero extra space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: O(1) space two-pointer linked list intersection algorithm on parent pointers.
